title: Harness Engineering: How to Build a Software Factory — Dru Knox, Tessl
talk_summary: Dru Knox frames 'harness engineering' as building three nested loops around coding agents: a cheap inner loop before PR, an expensive outer loop on PR, and a meta loop that mines logs/PRs/feedback to feed fixes back into the first two. He argues the prerequisite is a legible control plane (issues → headless sandboxed agent → PR comments) plus a skills registry, so all agent touchpoints are recorded and optimizable.

takeaways.what_they_do: Split agent checks by cost and cadence: cheap fast checks run continuously inside the agent's pre-PR iteration; expensive exhaustive checks (agentic QA, mutation testing) run once when the PR opens; a meta loop observes logs/PRs/feedback and pushes learnings back into the inner and outer loops.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the outer loop... where you might say like run mutation testing to check the quality of our test suite

takeaways.technique: Mutation testing as outer-loop review substitute
takeaways.what_they_do: Use mutation testing on the PR to measure whether the test suite actually catches injected defects, replacing human verification of test quality.
takeaways.evidence_quote: run mutation testing to check the quality of our test suite

takeaways.what_they_do: Central registry where workflows/playbooks are published, versioned, security- and quality-reviewed, with controls on who can publish, then distributed to all agents.
takeaways.evidence_quote: a skills registry where you can publish and version the workflows and the automations that you're working on with built-in governance

takeaways.technique: Mine PRs/issues for repeated tasks, then automate one at a time
takeaways.what_they_do: An agent scans PRs and issues to find recurring manual work (e.g. weekly flaky-test hunts) and converts each into a skill scheduled as an automated workflow, one workflow at a time.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the agent will mine through PRs, issues, things like that and find like every week you do a hunt for flaky tests

takeaways.technique: Track manual-takeover and human-comment rates as factory metrics
takeaways.what_they_do: Measure progress by driving down human PR comments and manual takeovers, and increasing PRs initiated without human input, holding quality constant first.
takeaways.evidence_quote: driving down manual takeovers, driving down human PR comments

takeaways.technique: Headless sandboxed agents with PR-comment interface
takeaways.what_they_do: All work starts as an issue, goes to a headless agent in a sandbox with appropriate permissions and a GitHub token, which opens a PR and responds to comments — making every touchpoint legible and long-running-capable.
takeaways.evidence_quote: It gets sent to a headless agent running in a sandbox. The agent puts up a PR
